# Labour Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## Core Vision: Britain Only Succeeds When Working People Succeed

The 2015 Labour manifesto presents a vision of national renewal built on the principle that economic prosperity must be shared by all, not concentrated among a privileged few. It offers a fundamental critique of Conservative governance while positioning Labour as the party of work, family, and community.

## Fiscal Responsibility with Fairness

Labour commits to a "Budget Responsibility Lock" guaranteeing every policy is fully funded without additional borrowing. The party pledges to cut the deficit annually and achieve a budget surplus as soon as possible. However, unlike Conservative austerity, Labour proposes fairer choices: restoring the 50p top tax rate for those earning over £150,000, abolishing non-dom status, and closing tax loopholes exploited by the wealthy while protecting ordinary working families from tax increases.

## An Economy for Working People

The manifesto diagnoses a broken link between national prosperity and family living standards, with wages falling dramatically since 2010. Labour's solution includes raising the minimum wage to over £8 by 2019, banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, and promoting the Living Wage. A British Investment Bank would support small businesses, while industrial strategy would create a million green jobs and position Britain as a leader in low-carbon technology.

## Investing in Public Services

Labour promises to "rescue" the NHS through £2.5 billion additional investment, funded by a Mansion Tax on properties over £2 million. This would deliver 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses, and 3,000 midwives. Mental health would receive equal priority with physical health. Education spending would be protected, tuition fees cut to £6,000, and every qualified school-leaver guaranteed an apprenticeship.

## Supporting Families and Communities

The manifesto addresses the housing crisis by committing to 200,000 new homes annually by 2020, three-year tenancies for private renters, and abolition of the "cruel" Bedroom Tax. Childcare would expand from 15 to 25 hours for working parents, and paternity leave would double.

## Controlled Immigration with Fair Rules

While acknowledging immigration's contributions, Labour proposes stronger borders, a two-year wait before EU migrants can claim benefits, and laws preventing employers from undercutting wages through worker exploitation.

## Devolving Power

Labour promises the biggest devolution in a century through an English Devolution Act transferring £30 billion to city and county regions, implementation of the Smith Agreement for Scotland, and a Constitutional Convention to reform Westminster, including replacing the House of Lords with an elected Senate.

## Britain in the World

The manifesto champions EU membership as essential for jobs and security while committing to reform. Labour pledges to maintain strong armed forces, uphold the 0.7% international development commitment, and lead global action on climate change toward net-zero emissions.

This manifesto presents Labour's vision of a more equal, democratically accountable Britain where prosperity is built together and shared fairly.
